name: EnnoDB
tagline: Deliberately naive C key-value store served over FastCGI, built on a crit-bit tree and an append-only log.
description: EnnoDB is a tiny hobby key-value database written in C by Enno Rehling and published in June 2015; its own README warns against using it for anything serious. It runs as a FastCGI application behind a web server such as nginx, exposing keys under a /k/ endpoint for get and set and a /l/ endpoint for listing keys by prefix. Data lives in memory in a crit-bit tree, and every write is appended to a binary log that is replayed on start-up, with an optional read-only mode set from an .ini file. Versions 1.0 through 1.4 all shipped within ten days in June 2015, and the repository has been idle since 2016. It is a compact example of a log-structured in-memory store, not a production system.
statusNote: Hobby project; versions 1.0-1.4 released in June 2015, no commits since 2016.
strengths: Very small, readable C codebase: crit-bit index plus append-only log
Prefix listing comes for free from the crit-bit tree
weaknesses: Author explicitly says not to use it for serious projects
Whole dataset must fit in RAM and the log is never compacted
No authentication, replication or concurrency guarantees
useCases: Learning how log-replay key-value stores work
Toy HTTP key-value service behind nginx
